rules.R1_pin_binding: A statement whose own text carries a revision qualifier (`at <rev>`) is scored AT THAT REVISION (entries carrying a `pin`). The pin is taken from the cited base line and is never moved to REV (R44C2Sentinel B1).
rules.R2_current_observable: The `## Owned axes` rows are the lane's CURRENT observable: their own Evidence cell names the counting command (tools/round-38/c2-counter.py, whose O1/O2 checks compare the row's count with command A at the scored revision) and their Last-change cell records the rounds at which the count was refreshed. Those rows are therefore scored against the FREEZE tree, so a sibling landing after the freeze (C1's knowledge entry) cannot move the number under them.
rules.R3_no_note_is_evidence: An appended `<!-- c2-correction: <id> -->` block declares a value; it never proves one. A check's observation is the statement's value only when it EQUALS the independently derived value; otherwise the observation is `UNSUPPORTED:<statement value>` and the entry stays a mismatch (R44C2Sentinel B3, hard rule).
rules.R4_two_sources: Every check has a second source of truth: the value is re-derived from git objects (command A, a heading range, a committed receipt, a marker), never by grepping the file that carries the claim.
rules.R5_append_only_repair: Repairs are append-only. The rubric binds the exact appended block (`expected_edits`) and the cited lines' sha256 digests (`preserve`); nothing may be edited in place or deleted.
rules.R6_pinned_clauses_stay: A pinned clause is immutable history: its repair is a NEW dated statement (the appended correction block), never a rewrite of the pinned cell.
rules.R7_read_only: Checks read git objects only: no network, no REA, no execution of committed code, no writes, and nothing outside the exported tree and the scratch clone (HYAKU_REPO).

check_contract.command: the entry's `command` argv; {rev}, {freeze} and {repo} are substituted by the counter; the command runs with cwd = the exported tree of REV and env HYAKU_REPO = the scratch clone (the only path source a check may use)
check_contract.output: one JSON object on stdout: {"observed": <value>, "derived": <value>, "detail": <text>}; the counter reads `observed` (observed_key)
check_contract.observation_rule: observed = the statement's value at REV when it equals the independent derivation, else "UNSUPPORTED:" + the statement's value
check_contract.script_pinning: every command embeds its check script; `check_script_sha256` is the sha256 of that script text, so a drifted script is detectable by the counter or by any reviewer (R44C2Sentinel B4, adapted to the counter's `command` schema, which has no script-file field)
check_contract.fitness: every entry is shown able to fail on its own statement: the base census scores each entry against the base blob, and the entries' `asserted` values are the independently derived ones (a rubric that copied the file's own value would report `UNSUPPORTED:<file value>` and stay a mismatch).

frozen_paths_note: corpus/README.md is deliberately NOT byte-frozen: C1's landing appends a coverage-map row to it, so a byte-frozen README would make a correct C1 landing a `frozen_path_changed` exit 2 for C2. The three README entries (C2-h1/h2/h3) derive at the FREEZE tree and locate their statements by content, so C1's row cannot move them; each README entry also carries the sha256 of the base line it cites. NOTE: the counter applies C2_DEFAULT_FROZEN unconditionally, so this declaration only takes effect if the counter honours the rubric's frozen_paths (the counter author's change) or the score is taken at a REV before C1's README landing (the L1's sequencing).
